_about: The dashboard To-Do feed. Refreshed at every Rule 9 checkpoint alongside the session handoff — this is the handoff distilled into plain language for the 📋 button on every tab. Split For Sam (curation / decisions only a human makes) and For Fable (engineering, the next session picks up).
_status: SkyView got three rounds of scrutiny on 2026-09-06 and came out of all three with real fixes. A computer-use session logged sixteen findings: four were genuine and are fixed — the details panel no longer drops you into the middle of a course you just opened, there is now a way back from a course to its discipline (Escape only ever worked if you had arrived by keyboard), every discipline stopped paying a wasted failed download before its descriptions load, and the M-ID chip explains what it means. Two of its findings were not defects at all, and the one it ranked most serious was wrong in an instructive way: it 'corrected' a figure that was already right for the file it named, having measured a different one. Sam then drove SkyView himself and reported five more: hovering a college course showed the same card every time, the background turned purple when you picked something, typing one more letter of 'welding' made the main intro course vanish from the search, the side panel reopened itself after you hid it, and the results list stopped at 60. All five are fixed, and the panel now also lists similar courses in level order, beginning before advanced. Sam then answered a seven-item decision sheet in one sitting — every one 'yes' — so the search chips are now navigable, the whole panel row opens its course, a carried course can be dropped on a destination in the panel, the view button names what it recentres on, Enter leaves the results list up, there is a skip link to the map, and the daily run rebuilds SkyView's decision data so a curator is never offered a decision about a course that no longer exists. Separately, three GitHub Actions workflows were using 89% of the repo's build minutes and are now trimmed. What is still open: the course outline itself, still unbuilt, and one question only Sam can answer — how three sources of skill statements are reconciled when they disagree.

items.text: You ruled 'All three' on where agency skill statements come from — published agency standards, ACE exhibits, and entered by the MAP team — and flagged it for follow-up. The open question is what wins when the three disagree about the same certification. That answer shapes the course outline's comparison panel, so the next session will need it early.

Three welding merge candidates are queued for a faculty reviewer, not for a session: Introduction to Welding (24 colleges) absorbing Introduction to the Welding Processes (2) and Intro-Welding Processes (1), and the Intermediate Shielded Metal Arc Welding pair behind it. A fourth pair shares a title but is flagged as NOT mergeable — one is credit and one is noncredit, which makes them different courses. kb/merge_candidates/2026-09-05/report.md.

The re-mint approval view is designed and routed through Governance, not built. You approve candidates and the cron applies them; there is no fire button, because a re-mint cannot be undone the way an ordinary correction can. Worth a read before it is built — it names what each candidate must show you, including what the plan was checked against, which is exactly the thing that was missing this week.

Build the course outline on double-click: a layered panel with the MAP-Generated label on every synthetic field, proficiency levels on the course and on each skill, thin skills kept with a confidence chip, and a certification-first way in beside the course-first one. Double-click currently opens the discipline work surface, so split it — a course opens the outline, empty ground keeps today's behavior.

Build the re-mint approval queue against the four-item checklist in its decision record: a register row owning the approval, the surface mapped the moment the first write lands, an insert-only rollback, and a test asserting the view writes approvals and nothing else.
docs/roadmap_archive.md is 575 KB against a 150 KB budget — the largest thing the docs lint flags, and pure history. It is a safe compaction whenever a session has spare room.

The panel's new Similar courses list reads course levels out of titles, which is the only place we hold them — 44% of Welding's 512 titles say Beginning, Intermediate or Advanced and the rest are listed last rather than guessed at. When the course outline ships with a real level field, feed it back here so the ladder stops depending on wording.
